summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, poorly controlled HIV/AIDS (CD4=13, viral load 1,250), and a history of MRSA bacteremia presented after missing two dialysis sessions due to foot pain from a mechanical fall. She fell on her front steps, stubbing her left great toe, which caused significant pain and limited mobility. Initial labs showed hyperkalemia (K=5.7) and elevated creatinine (11.5), with hypotension (BP 79/38) attributed to her baseline low blood pressure and upper extremity scarring affecting readings. Imaging revealed no fractures in the toe or hip. She underwent three hemodialysis sessions during admission, with improvement in electrolytes and symptoms. Pain was managed with a fentanyl patch and a surgical shoe. Her warfarin was continued for presumed DVT, and medications for secondary hyperparathyroidism were maintained. She was discharged home with home health support, follow-up plans, and instructions for medication adherence and dialysis attendance.
